ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an equilateral triangle, with the base horizontal, and two squares of different sizes inside. The larger square on the left is placed obliquely, and 70° is marked between its upper side and the left side of the equilateral triangle. The smaller square on the right has one side attached to the right side of the equilateral triangle. The angle marked with the question mark is located between the right side of the larger square and the upper side of the smaller square. Reasoning: Take the base of the equilateral triangle as a horizontal line, then the direction of the left side is 60°, and the right side as an undirected straight line has direction 120°. The 70° in the figure is the angle between the left-side direction 60° and the upper side of the large square, so the direction of the upper side of the large square is 60° - 70° = -10°. The right side of the large square is perpendicular to its upper side, so its direction is -10° + 90° = 80°. The small square has one side along the right side of the equilateral triangle, with direction 120°, and its adjacent upper side is perpendicular to that side, so its direction is 120° - 90° = 30°. The question-mark angle is the included angle between the right side of the large square with direction 80° and the upper side of the small square with direction 30°, so it is 80° - 30° = 50°.

Extend the larger square’s top side until it meets the right side of the equilateral triangle. Now use perpendicular transfer: the side of the larger square involved in the question mark is perpendicular to the larger square’s top side, and the side of the smaller square involved in the question mark is perpendicular to the right side of the triangle because the adjacent side of the smaller square lies along that triangle side.
